html:
The Emberá Chamí are a branch of the Emberá people living on the eastern slopes of the Western Cordillera of the Andes in Colombia, in Risaralda, Caldas, Antioquia and Valle del Cauca. They speak Chamí, an Emberá language.

They farm maize, plantains and coffee on the steep slopes, and are known for colourful beadwork. In the colonial period the Spanish drew them into gold mining and missions. In the 1900s settlers and coffee farms took much of their land, and in recent decades the armed conflict in Colombia has displaced many of them to the cities. Their neighbours to the west include the Wounaan.
